To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Centiloid conversion successfully converts quantitative amyloide imaging measurements into comparable values with a common dynamic range.

(1) The Centiloid scale is useful for cross-sectional and longitudinal analysis of amyloid imaging PET data; (2) Differences in the variability and mean values of amyloid burden measurements obtained using different analytical approaches are reflected in Centiloid values; and (3) When amyloid measurements from different centers are pooled for analysis, the differences in the underlying acquisition protocol and analysis methodology are not fully eliminated by the Centiloid transformation.

the Centiloid approach can be successfully used to convert quantitative amyloid imaging measurements into a common scale and that even after conversion into Centiloids, differences in the amyloid burden measurements obtained from different analytical approaches can remain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the Centiloid method and the evaluation of the impact of the underlying analysis methodology on the Centiloid conversion.
the use of the Centiloid approach for cross-sectional and longitudinal analysis of PET amyloid imaging data.
the impact of different image analysis techniques on the Centiloid approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Centiloid approach does not eliminate all the differences between different analysis methods.
Centiloid conversion does not eliminate all differences in underlying analytical approaches, and therefore, the Centiloids obtained from different centers cannot be considered as equivalent.
Centiloid conversion is an important step in the process of combining amyloid measurements from different sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Centiloids provide a common standard to compare amyloid burden across studies, but they do not provide the same level of standardization that is achieved by a common acquisition protocol.

the Centiloid conversion is a valuable tool in cross-sectional and especially longitudinal amyloid imaging studies, and that the Centiloids derived from different analytical pipelines are not identical.

Centiloid approach is an important and valuable step towards standardization of amyloid imaging quantification, however, the variability in the underlying analysis methodologies is not eliminated by this approach.
